name: Garment and knitwear export units

problems.words: We missed the ex-factory date and had to air-ship at our own cost
quick_ideas: Put every live order's ex-factory date and current stage on one page, so you see which ones are already at risk
Go back through the last missed shipment and note the milestone that slipped first, so you know where to watch

workzap_build.text: An order and TNA board for every style with milestone dates and status, flagging at-risk orders automatically each morning for merchandisers and the owner.

problems.ask_first: At which stage do orders usually slip?
problems.free_stops: Which milestones are tracked and how risk flags are triggered is set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the planned and actual date for each recent internal handover on the missed order, so the earliest slip stands out.
Give one person the job of updating one wall sheet at the same time daily, so risky orders get chased earlier.

problems.words: Fabric arrived late from the mill so stitching started late
quick_ideas: List every open fabric and trims PO with promised and actual arrival dates, so you see which supplier slips most
Mark which ship dates depend on each late PO, so the knock-on is visible straight away

workzap_build.text: A material arrival tracker per order with PO, promised and received dates, sending shortage and delay alerts linked to the ship date.

problems.ask_first: Which arrives late most often — fabric, trims or accessories?
problems.free_stops: How material delays are tied to each order's ship date is mapped in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note for each late fabric lot how many days passed between promise and arrival, so the worst mill delays are clear.
Give one store staff member one notebook for all expected fabric arrivals, so late lots get flagged before stitching waits.

problems.words: Merchandisers keep the TNA in their own Excel and I can't see all orders
quick_ideas: Ask each merchandiser to share their order list once into one shared file, so you have a single view for the first time
Agree the handful of milestones every merchandiser must report, so updates look the same

workzap_build.text: One shared order board that every merchandiser updates, so the owner sees all styles on one screen and order knowledge stays when people leave.

problems.free_stops: The board layout and who updates what are covered in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many live orders you can see without asking merchandisers individually, so the visibility gap shows.
Give one coordinator one master order list kept in one place, so you can review all live orders together.

problems.words: Line efficiency varies a lot and I don't know why
quick_ideas: Have one line record output every hour for a day, so you see when it drops
Note what was happening at each drop (machine, feeding, style change), so causes are on record

workzap_build.text: Hourly line output entered on phone by the line in-charge, with efficiency against SMV shown live and summarised daily by line.

problems.ask_first: How is line output recorded during the day?
problems.free_stops: How efficiency is calculated per style and line is detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare output, style and helper availability across two lines on one shift, so likely reasons for variation stand out.
Give one supervisor the job of noting stoppage reasons in one notebook each shift, so line discussions use facts.

problems.words: Defects are found at the end, not inline
quick_ideas: Put one checker inline on your worst line for a day, so you see where defects start
Note the top three defects from the last failed inspection, so checking focuses on them

workzap_build.text: An inline and final QC app recording defects by type, operation and line with photos, summarised daily so rework is caught early.

problems.free_stops: Defect categories and where checkpoints sit are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count defects found inline versus at final check for one busy line, so you see where detection is failing.
Give one checker one fixed mid-shift walk on the same line daily, so defects get noticed before piles build up.

problems.words: Cutting wastage is higher than the costing allowed
quick_ideas: For one style, compare fabric issued to cutting against pieces cut and the costing allowance, so you see the real gap
Count leftover fabric and panels in the cutting room once, so you know what is sitting there

workzap_build.text: A cutting register comparing fabric issued, pieces cut and costing allowance per style, with leftovers logged.

problems.free_stops: How allowances are set and compared per style is set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare leftover fabric rolls and cut panel bundles from one completed style with its costing allowance, so excess loss is clear.
Give one cutting staff member one place to note leftover fabric by style, so repeat wastage stops being guessed.

problems.words: Subcontractor delivered fewer pieces than we sent cut panels for
quick_ideas: Reconcile panels sent and pieces received for each current subcontractor once, so you know who owes what
Ask for a signed count on the next return, so disputes start small

workzap_build.text: A subcontractor ledger for pieces sent, received, rejected and paid, flagging any shortfall the day goods come back.

problems.free_stops: How counts are confirmed and linked to payment is covered in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count bundles sent out and pieces returned for each current subcontract job once, so the largest shortage is clear.
Give one dispatch person one handover page for sent and returned counts, so piece disputes are checked from one record.

problems.words: Buyer deducted a claim and we don't know what for
quick_ideas: List every claim and deduction this year against its shipment, so patterns show up
Ask the buyer for the reason on each open deduction, so nothing is written off blind

workzap_build.text: A buyer payment and claims tracker with ageing and the reason for each deduction, linked to the shipment.

problems.ask_first: How are claims and deductions tracked today?
problems.free_stops: How claims are matched to shipments and followed up is kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note each buyer deduction beside the shipment issue mentioned in your papers, so you see which record is missing.
Give one office person one notebook page for every deduction and related shipment note, so follow-up stops getting lost.

problems.words: I don't know the real margin per style once rework and air freight are in
quick_ideas: For your last shipped style, put actual fabric, rework and freight next to the costing, so the real margin shows
Pick the style you underquoted last and note what was missed, so the next costing includes it

workzap_build.text: A costing tool that compares actual against costing after every shipment, per style.

problems.free_stops: Which actual costs are captured and how is detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare costing notes with actual rework, extra freight and fabric use on one recent style, so hidden margin loss appears.
Give one merchandiser one place to note extra costs by style as they happen, so margin review is based on actuals.

problems.words: No proper catalogue or website for new buyers to see our capability
quick_ideas: Gather good photos of your lines, products and past styles in one folder, so you have something to send
Write down what new buyers ask to see first, so the catalogue answers it

workzap_build.text: A simple capability website and digital lookbook that new buyers can browse and enquire from.

problems.free_stops: The structure and content of the site are planned in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many recent style photos clearly show fabric, stitching and finishing, so you see what capability proof is still missing.
Give one merchandiser one notebook page for buyer-ready style photos and factory shots, so sending capability stops getting delayed.

never_say: Anything on social-compliance audits, certifications or how to pass them; never help create or alter attendance, wage or working-hour records.
Any advice on LCs, export finance, duty drawback, customs or tax refunds; suggest an accountant or banker.
Any help with fake origin labels, misdeclared quantities or under-invoicing.
Any help optimising child labour, forced overtime or withheld wages.
Any judgement on who is liable in a buyer claim; note the record gap only.
Any guarantee of on-time shipment or higher efficiency.

sample_reply.person: We keep missing ex-factory because fabric comes late, and I only find out when it's too late. What can we do?
sample_reply.pi: Yes, this can be brought under control, and you can start this week. 1) List every open fabric and trims order with its promised and actual arrival date, so you can see which supplier slips most. 2) Next to each one, mark the ship date that depends on it, so a delay shows its knock-on straight away. Workzap can do this automatically for you: a material tracker tied to each order's TNA that alerts you the day fabric slips and shows every at-risk ship date each morning. Shall I prepare a solution document and quote for you? You're welcome to say no.
